headline: Vilon
punch: The one in this family with a real animal outcome.

headline: What it actually is
body: **Lys-Glu**, a two amino acid peptide. Khavinson's thymus and immune targeted bioregulator, and the simplest molecule in the whole family. | Two residues is as short as a peptide gets before it stops being one. Which makes the family's central claim, that these bind DNA at specific promoter sequences, hardest to defend here: there is almost no molecule to do the binding with.
punch: Two amino acids. The shortest claim to make.

headline: It has an outcome study
body: This is the thing that separates Vilon from its relatives. Female CBA mice were given **0.1 microgram subcutaneously, 5 consecutive days per month, starting at 6 months of age**. | Mean lifespan increased **about 16%**, and spontaneous tumour incidence was reduced against controls. That is a hard outcome, not a marker, and it is the strongest single result in this family.
punch: Lifespan +16%. Tumours down. A real endpoint.

headline: Note the dose
body: **0.1 microgram.** Not milligram. A tenth of a microgram, five days a month. | Set that against the 1 to 10 milligram daily figures circulating for human use of these compounds, which is four to five orders of magnitude higher on a per-dose basis before you adjust for body weight. The one dose with an outcome behind it is tiny and intermittent.
punch: ==The one effective dose was 0.1 µg, 5 days a month.==

headline: But it is an immune peptide
body: Vilon is thymus and immune targeted. The lifespan and tumour findings are consistent with an immune or anti-inflammatory effect in an ageing animal. | There is no growth plate data, no chondrocyte data, and no bone length endpoint anywhere in its literature. A lifespan effect in an old mouse is not evidence about a growing plate.
punch: Lifespan in an old mouse is not height in a growing one.

headline: Nothing replicated
body: The whole family has essentially **no peer-reviewed efficacy evidence outside a small Russian literature that has not been internationally replicated**. | And the core mechanistic claim, that di- and tripeptides bind DNA with sequence specificity, is **considered biologically implausible by Western molecular biology standards** and has been replicated by **no independent laboratory**.
punch: One lab, one country, forty years, no replication.

headline: The dose has no PK
body: Circulating human dose figures for this family are **not grounded in pharmacokinetic studies**. Every documented human regimen is a pulsed course of 10 to 30 days. | So the human dosing is a tradition inherited from a research programme, not a calculation from measured absorption and clearance. The mouse number is the only one with an outcome attached and it is not a human number.
punch: The human dose is inherited, not derived.

headline: Intranasal is untested
body: One genuinely interesting point in its favour. A 2022 review proposes that 2 to 4 residue peptides are small enough to use real transporters, the **POT family** PEPT1/2 and PHT1/2, plus LAT1/2. | POT transporters are expressed in **human nasal epithelium**, which gives a transporter-level rationale for intranasal delivery rather than a marketing one. But **zero head-to-head injectable versus intranasal comparisons exist**.
punch: A real transport rationale. No comparison study.

headline: It is chemically robust
body: Vilon carries no free thiol, no oxidisable aromatic residues and low reactive valence, which makes it one of the most chemically inert compounds in this space. | It is very stable as dry powder and can be co-reconstituted and co-stored with its relatives without degrading them. Whatever else is true, handling and storage are not where this one fails.
punch: Stable, inert, and easy to store.

headline: Probably harmless
body: At typical doses these peptides are expected to be **hydrolysed into common dietary amino acids**, which is why the family is rated **low risk of harm** even by people who reject the mechanism outright. | Lysine and glutamate are two of the most ordinary amino acids in your diet. The honest risk framing is wasted money rather than damage.
punch: You are most likely eating lysine and glutamate.

headline: Verdict
body: The only member of this family with a hard animal outcome: 16% lifespan extension and reduced tumour incidence in mice, at 0.1 micrograms five days a month. That is worth knowing and it is worth not overstating. | It is an immune peptide with no growth plate, chondrocyte or bone length data of any kind, from an unreplicated literature, at human doses with no pharmacokinetic basis.
punch: A real result, in the wrong tissue, at a tiny dose.
